$comment: The kinds of ledger CLPR can connect. status: documented = the ledger has a Ledger Specification in clpr-spec/ledgers/<specDir>/ledger.md (the index is clpr-spec/ledgers/README.md); code = verifier code exists in clpr-smart-contracts without a Ledger Specification, and the row's text keeps to what the code's own documents say; mock = a stand-in. check-data.mjs fails when a ledger directory or a verifier code directory upstream has no row here.

ledgers.name: Hiero networks, public and private
ledgers.proof: Paths into the network's state under a threshold signature of its nodes on the block root. Two proof schemes: Hiero receivers also check a proof that ties the signing key to the ledger's fixed identity; EVM receivers follow the signing key as the node roster changes
ledgers.service: A native service of the ledger

refs.label: Hiero proof scheme: hinTS with WRAPS

ledgers.name: An EVM ledger that reaches consensus with QBFT
ledgers.proof: A block header carrying the validators' seals, plus a proof of the CLPR Service contract's storage that holds the data. Three proof schemes differ in where the validator set comes from: epoch boundary headers, every block header, or a validator contract
ledgers.endpoint: Registered endpoints; under the recommended design, the CLPR Service administrator admits them

ledgers.name: Ethereum mainnet
ledgers.proof: Sync-committee signatures checked by a light client

ledgers.name: Tempo, an EVM ledger with threshold-signature finality
ledgers.proof: A finalization certificate: one threshold signature by the validators over the block, plus a proof of the storage slots that hold the data
ledgers.endpoint: None: the endpoint program does not support it

ledgers.name: Avalanche
ledgers.proof: Not implemented; a mock verifier stands in
ledgers.endpoint: None: the endpoint program does not support it
